wizard.title: New project
wizard.lede: Describe a topic, ask your questions, declare the sources and the bar. Claimstone checks each step and keeps a draft. Nothing runs while you fill in these steps, and creating the project starts nothing either: research begins only in a later stage, after you authorize it.
wizard.signIn: Sign in to create a project.

explain.title: What Claimstone will do
explain.afterStart: After you start research (next stage of the portal)

kind.effect: effect — judged on results that test it: estimates, uncertainty, time horizon, sample, study design.
kind.heterogeneity: heterogeneity — judged on the contrast between subgroups, with its uncertainty and whether the subgroup analysis was prespecified.
kind.method: method — judged on which sources endorse the practice and which demonstrate its failure, kept apart, each with the role of its source.
kind.premise: premise — judged on the explicit statement of it, or a contradiction of it.
kind.operational: operational — tracked in this project; no literature verdict applies, and it is never shown as awaiting your signature.

step1.title: 1 · The topic
step1.intro: Name the project and list what to search for. Terms are broad on purpose: their job is to find works, not to define what is learned.
step1.name: Project name
step1.nameHelp: 2 to 63 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens, starting with a letter or a digit. It becomes the folder name and cannot be changed.
step1.descriptionHelp: A free note for whoever reads the project later: what is in scope and out, in a few sentences. These are not the questions to answer — you write those in step 2. No stage of the analysis reads this note.
step1.termsHelp: Each term is searched as written.
step1.afterSave: Claimstone checks the name and the topics, then keeps a draft. Nothing is created and nothing runs.
step1.atCreation: Your topics and terms are written to topics.yaml. Later, each term becomes one search on each index you choose when you authorize a plan. So far — topics: {topics}, terms: {terms}, searches per index: {searches}, with all three indexes: {searchesAll}.
step1.afterStart: Terms find works; they do not define what is learned. A wider topic finds more candidates, and every candidate found adds to the denominator the acquisition floor is measured against.

step2.title: 2 · The questions
step2.intro: This step is the list of questions Claimstone must answer, one per row; they get the numbers Q01, Q02… Write each literature question as a statement the literature can support or contradict. Claimstone does not judge your wording: it only checks that a question is not empty and has a kind.
step2.question: Question
step2.afterSave: Claimstone checks each question and keeps a draft. The questions are not frozen yet, so you can still change them.
step2.atCreation: The question registry is frozen at version 1 on the day you create the project (UTC date). Questions: {total} (literature: {literature}, operational: {operational}). Literature questions can receive a verdict, and only a person signs one; operational questions are tracked but never receive one. Changing the registry later needs a dated new version, never a silent edit.
step2.afterStart: Each kind is judged by its own rule. Claimstone reads sources with these questions in mind and extracts claims, each bound to a verbatim quote that code checks character by character. If a round clears the floor, each literature question gets an evidence profile; a person reads it and signs one of five states: SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED, CONTESTED_IN_LITERATURE, UNANSWERED_IN_LITERATURE or NEVER_ASKED. "Found nothing" is never reported as "no effect".

step3.title: 3 · Sources and rigour
step3.intro: Declare which kinds of source may count and the bar a round must clear before it can conclude anything. Both are declared now and recorded on the day you create the project (UTC date).
step3.technicalHelp: Defaults suit most projects: the notation for outcome values and extra hosts never to contact.
step3.classesHelp: Every source carries its class, and classes are never mixed silently. Choose at least one.
step3.floorHelp: The share of found works that must be obtained as confirmed copies. Above 0 and at most 1, for example 0.80 = 80%.
step3.rationaleHelp: At least 20 characters. A bar without a reason is a bar somebody can move.
step3.suppliedCount: Count toward the floor once verified
step3.suppliedSeparate: Read them, but report them separately from the floor

suppliedValue.count: count — counted toward the floor once verified
suppliedValue.separate: separate — read, but reported apart from the floor

step3.suppliedHelp: Declared now, before any copy exists, and it cannot change while this protocol holds.
step3.notation: How your discipline writes its figures
step3.customLabelsHelp: For example the abbreviations a paper writes next to a number.
step3.hosts: Hosts never to contact, besides the standing list
step3.hostsHelp: One bare host name per line, no https://, path or wildcard.
step3.afterSave: Claimstone checks the classes, the floor and its reason, and keeps a draft.
step3.atCreation: The floor {floor} is written with your reason, dated the day you create the project (UTC date), and admits no override. Source classes chosen: {classes}; every source will carry one of them. Excluded hosts are never contacted (added by you: {added}). Copies you supply: {supplied}.
step3.afterStart: After the search, Claimstone counts how many of the works it found it could obtain as confirmed copies. Below the floor it marks the round INSUFFICIENT_ACQUISITION: no evidence profile is built and no verdict can be signed. A corpus read at 42% that certifies itself complete is worse than no corpus.

step4.title: 4 · Review and create
step4.intro: This is exactly what will be created. Check it, then confirm.
step4.summary: Project: {name} · Topics: {topics} · Questions: {total} (literature {literature}, operational {operational}) · Source classes: {classes} · Floor: {floor}
step4.needSteps: Steps 1 to 3 must be saved before you can review the project.
step4.files: The files that will be created
step4.digest: Protocol fingerprint (sha256): what you see is what is created
step4.advancedHelp: An edit replaces a whole file and must still load with the same checks. If you change an earlier step after editing here, reset the files so they are generated again.
step4.resetHelp: If you edited the files and the UTC date has changed since, reset them so they are generated again.
step4.unsaved: You have unsaved file changes: save or discard them first.
step4.confirm: I understand that the question registry and the floor are frozen at version 1 on {frozenAt} (UTC date), and that changing them later needs a dated new version.
step4.startNote: Not available yet: authorizing and starting research comes with the next stage of the portal.
step4.notStarted: Creating the project starts no search, no copy request and no model call, and spends nothing.
step4.privacy: The project is created in the projects/ folder, which Git ignores: it stays on this machine and is not published.
step4.next1: You will authorize one exact plan (searches, copy requests, any paid model work) before anything runs.
step4.next2: Claimstone searches the indexes and obtains legal copies, recording every attempt.
step4.next3: It prepares the documents and extracts claims bound to verbatim quotes, and an independent second reader reviews each one.
step4.next4: If the round clears the floor, it builds an evidence profile for each literature question.
step4.next5: A person reads each profile and signs a verdict. No verdict is signed for you.
step4.afterSave: Here you save only Advanced file edits: they are checked with the same loaders and kept in the draft. Nothing is created until you press "Create the project".
step4.atCreation: Claimstone writes three files under projects/{name}/, freezes the question registry and the floor at version 1 on {frozenAt} (UTC date), and records each file's hash. It starts nothing.
step4.afterStart: You will authorize one exact plan before anything runs. Claimstone then searches, obtains legal copies, prepares the documents, extracts claims bound to verbatim quotes, has an independent second reader review each one and, if the round clears the floor, builds an evidence profile per literature question. A person reads it and signs. This version of the portal does none of that yet.

created.title: Project created
created.body: The project {name} now exists, frozen at version 1 on {frozenAt} (UTC date). Nothing has started.
created.bodyUndated: The project {name} now exists, frozen at version 1. Nothing has started.

errors.VALIDATION: Some of what you entered cannot be accepted.
errors.STALE_REVISION: This draft was changed elsewhere. Reload it to see the latest version.
errors.DRAFT_CLOSED: This draft is closed: it was discarded or already turned into a project, so it can no longer be changed.
errors.PREVIEW_CHANGED: The draft changed after you opened this review, so what you confirmed is no longer what would be created. Reload to review the current version.
errors.NAME_TAKEN: A project with this name already exists. Go back to step 1 and choose another name.
errors.INCOMPLETE: The draft is not complete yet: steps 1 to 3 must all be saved first.
errors.UNAUTHORIZED: Your session has ended. Sign in again, then repeat the action.

login.title: Sign in
login.lede: Reading needs no session. Signing, deciding and exporting do.
